hook: A massive 1,500-kilometer object just appeared in the dark shadows beyond Pluto.

sections.voiceover: A massive 1,500-kilometer object just appeared in the dark shadows beyond Pluto.
sections.visual_cue: Deep space starfield panning toward a distant, cold, dark orbit.

sections.voiceover: Astronomers at the NSF-DOE Vera C. This trans-Neptunian object 2026 ED138 orbits far beyond the icy path of Pluto.
sections.visual_cue: Map showing Chile and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory location.

sections.voiceover: But researchers used the linking code pointdexter to identify this massive object from observatory data.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of digital telescope data streaming on a screen.

sections.voiceover: Scientists Matthew J. This object spans a range of 600 to 1,500 kilometers beyond the orbit of Pluto.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic scale comparison showing 600 to 1,500 kilometers.

sections.voiceover: The International Astronomical Union Minor Planet Center continues tracking this massive 2026 ED138.
sections.visual_cue: Wide, cinematic shot of the outer solar system's darkness.
